question.worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(3,-\frac{17}{2})$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =(x-3)^{2}+{(y+\frac{17}{2})}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}-6x+9+{y}^{2}+17y+\frac{289}{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}-6x+{y}^{2}+17y+\frac{325}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y={x}^{2}-6x.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(y) & =y+{y}^{2}+17y+\frac{325}{4} \\  & ={y}^{2}+18y+\frac{325}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(y)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(y)=2y+18 & =0 \\ 2y & =-18 \\ y & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(y)=2>0.$ Therefore, $y=-9$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $y=-9.$
